title: Reduced neurogenesis in a mouse hypomagnetic experiment
claim: In a controlled study of adult male mice, long-term 0.29 µT exposure was associated with reduced adult hippocampal neurogenesis relative to a 55.26 µT local field.
scope: Specific laboratory exposure and experimental protocol
limits: Not a dose-response model; does not establish human outcomes or effects at typical terrestrial intensities.

title: Mouse cognition changed under experimental exposure
claim: The 2021 mouse study reported impairments in selected hippocampus-dependent learning and memory tasks; some findings improved after return to normal-field conditions.
limits: Does not mean a magnetic field is an on/off switch for cognition.

title: South Atlantic minimum decreased across Swarm epochs
claim: A Swarm-derived model found the minimum surface intensity fell from 22.430 µT in 2014.0 to 22.094 µT in 2025.0.
scope: Swarm-inferred core field at Earth mean spherical surface; two reported epochs
limits: Not a live station reading, not a global average, and not a measurement at a person's location.

title: WMM is a model rather than a biosensor
claim: NOAA WMM2025 estimates Earth's main magnetic-field components and secular variation, including total intensity F, from geography, altitude and date.
limits: WMM outputs should not be labeled live measurements.

title: ROS responses are cell and context dependent
claim: The 2021 study reported lower reactive oxygen species in adult neural stem cells under the studied hypomagnetic conditions, with changes in cell function.
scope: Neural stem cell ROS in the 2021 study
limits: Do not automatically generalize the direction of ROS change to every brain cell or experiment.

title: Mitochondria and iron-sulfur clusters are candidate mechanisms
claim: A 2026 review discusses mitochondrial function and iron-sulfur clusters as possible mediators of hypomagnetic effects.
limits: A proposed mechanism is not experimental confirmation of a unique causal pathway.

title: Molecular pathways may support reversibility
claim: A 2025 mouse/neural stem-cell experiment implicated GSK-3β and mTOR phosphorylation in field-dependent changes in stem-cell proliferation.
limits: Pathway implication does not prove direct magnetic sensing by either protein.

title: Effects may depend on organism and disease model
claim: A 2026 Pink1 neurodegeneration model study investigated hypomagnetic effects on lifespan, physical ability and mitochondrial metabolism.
limits: Cannot be generalized to healthy human populations or used as evidence that weaker fields are universally harmful or beneficial.

title: Neuroinflammation is discussed in a 2026 abstract
claim: The 2026 EGU abstract discusses oxidative stress and neuroinflammatory pathways under hypomagnetic experimental conditions.
limits: Abstract alone provides insufficient details to independently assess all experiments and strengths of inference.

title: Present field weakening is harming human brains
claim: It is not established that current changes in Earth's magnetic field cause impaired neurogenesis or cognitive decline in humans.
limits: Do not promote this as a demonstrated result or derive a human risk threshold from mouse hypomagnetic exposures.

title: Kp and IMF are not Earth surface field intensity
claim: NOAA SWPC's planetary Kp index has no units, while upstream interplanetary magnetic field Bt/Bz is reported in nanotesla. Neither may be interpreted as local terrestrial F in microtesla.
scope: NOAA SWPC product definitions and data units
limits: Do not infer regional surface magnetic strength, or biological risk, from Kp or upstream Bz.

title: NBG/DCF geomagnetic coupling remains a proposed computational hypothesis
claim: A potential NBG/DCF-based predictive model would require frozen parameters and independent, held-out comparisons against conventional geophysical baselines before a relationship could be asserted.
scope: Proposed test methodology, not an empirically observed relationship
limits: No independent validation or field-to-biological-causation result is claimed by the v0.2 preregistration editor.
